deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated layers.

(A) Header of a lemniscatic-function table (only the first rows are filled). Column 1 holds the argument t = 0.00, 0.01, ..., 0.38. The constant 1,31102878 is ϖ/2, half the lemniscate constant: ϖ = 2∫_0^1 dx/√(1-x^4) = 2.62205755..., so ϖ/2 = 1.31102878. The previous page also lists 1,31102878 and is headed 'Rechnungen die Lemniscata betreffend'. For t = 0.01 Gauss enters 0,01311029 = (ϖ/2)·0.01 in the column headed 1,31102878. He enters the same figure in the column headed 0, which is consistent with sl((ϖ/2)t): sl(x) = x - x^5/10 + ..., and the correction is about 4·10^-11. The last column is headed 1 and gives 1,0000000 at t = 0.01. This matches √(1 - sl^4) = sl'(x), which is 1 - O(x^4) ≈ 1 - 1.5·10^-8. The column headed 0 between the double rule is empty. The table was evidently abandoned after one row.

(B) Scratch work: least-squares fitting of straight lines to empirical readings. The boxed list holds 12 readings: 0, 8.9, 13.6, 17.9, 22.1, 26.1, 30.0, 33.9, 37.7, 41.4, 45.1, 48.7. The next page has a variant list: 8.9, 13.6, 18.0, 22.23, 26.2, 30.0, 33.8, 37.7, 41.6, 45.2, 48.6. The physical meaning is unidentified; the next page carries times and place initials. Gauss splits the readings into overlapping blocks of four, y_k for k = 0..3, and fits y_k ≈ a + k b by least squares. The normal equations are
  Σ y_k = 4a + 6b,
  Σ k y_k = 6a + 14b.
He solves them by halving the first equation and dividing the second by 3:
  2a + 3b = S0/2,
  2a + (14/3)b = S1/3.
Subtracting gives (5/3)b = S1/3 - S0/2, so 5b = 3(difference), and then a = (S0/2 - 3b)/2.

Block 3 (data 37.7, 41.6, 45.2, 48.6):
- S0 = 173.1.
- S1 = 41.6 + 90.4 + 145.8 = 277.8. He first wrote 325.8, then corrected it to 277; the previous page has '14p = 277,8'.
- S1/3 = 92.6 and S0/2 = 86.55; difference 6.05; 5b = 18.15, so b = 3.63.
- a = (86.55 - 10.89)/2 = 75.66/2 = 37.83, matching the scratch figures 8655, 1089, 7566, 37,83.
- Fitted values: 37.83, 41.46, 45.09, 48.72.

Block 2 (data 26.2, 30.0, 33.8, 37.7, i.e. the next-page values):
- S0 = 127.7.
- S1 = 30 + 67.6 + 113.1 = 210.7.
- S1/3 = 70.2333 and S0/2 = 63.85; difference 6.3833; 5b = 19.15, so b = 3.83.
- a = (63.85 - 11.49)/2 = 52.36/2 = 26.18 (scratch figures 6385, 1149, 5236).
- Fitted values: 26.18, 30.01, 33.84, 37.67.

Block 1 (data 13.6, 18.0, 22.23, 26.2, the next-page values; my identification):
- S0 = 80.03 and S1 = 141.06 (the next page shows '141').
- These give b = 4.203 and a = 13.703, i.e. 13.70, 17.90, 22.10, 26.30 with b = 4.20, as written.

The third-column table splices the fitted values into one smoothed series: 17.90, 22.10, 26.16, 30.04, 33.84, 37.75, 41.46, 45.09. Here 37.75 is the mean of 37.67 and 37.83. The values 26.16 and 30.04 appear to be adjusted junction values. First differences are listed alongside.

The figures 81,71 and 4,23, 25,38, 147,73, 36,93 are unresolved side computations. The one clear relation is 147.73/4 ≈ 36.93.
errors: The first value of Σ k y_k for block 3 was written 325.8; the correct value is 41.6+90.4+145.8 = 277.8, which Gauss corrects to '277'.
The value 92.6 (= 277.8/3) is written on the line '2a+3b='. It belongs to 2a+4⅔b; 2a+3b = 173.1/2 = 86.55, which is the value actually used in the subtraction.
The last difference in the third-column scratch reads 3,65; 45.09 - 41.46 = 3.63 (possibly a reading issue).

In the fifth column, 26.30 versus 26.18 and 37.67 versus 37.83 show that the separate block fits do not join continuously. This is not an error, just piecewise fitting; Gauss reconciles the joins in the third-column series.
